BACKGROUND

JusPrin is an AI-piloted fork of OrcaSlicer (C++17, wxWidgets). Its "Check print" window today is OrcaSlicer's stock G-code Preview dropped into a modal wxDialog (`CheckPrintDialog` in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/StatusRow.cpp`, built with `Plater::create_preview`), unchanged: a 14-row line-type legend, a vertical layer slider with number boxes, a horizontal moves slider. `agent-docs/jusprin/product-definition.md` section 2.8 says that is the expert view and the default should be a short risk report; the legend and layer count are "not beginner decision aids".

On 2026-10-21 Kenneth decided the redesign and it was drawn on the "JusPrin v2" design canvas (https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v), page id `check-print`, boards `check-print-01-default`, `check-print-02-legend-and-moves`, `check-print-03-finding-selected`, `check-print-04-report-states`. The decisions are also in `~/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/memory/check-print-design-decisions.md`.

Decisions: the window stays a modal over Prepare holding OrcaSlicer's real preview; a native report panel built from the existing `IWorkspace::slice_report` sits to the right of the preview; exactly two toggles, "Legend" and "Moves slider", each showing or hiding one OrcaSlicer overlay, both off when the window opens; OrcaSlicer's view-type dropdown lives inside its legend so it shows only with the legend; the vertical layer slider stays; both sliders are drawn in the brand's action colour while the bed and the legend keep OrcaSlicer's colours; closing the window (or Escape) is the only way back to Prepare, so the report has no fix button and no agent button. Not decided: whether the two toggles are remembered between openings (default: not remembered).

Design-system rules: every colour, radius, font and control size comes from the token file through `ShellTheme` and the shell recipes (`agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md`, "Writing UI code"); a value with no token gets a token and a guard first. Kenneth's rule for this screen: one-off values are fine only for elements unique to it (the 360 DIP panel width, the 48 DIP window header); everything shared uses tokens. Five tokens were added to the Design System artifact today and must be carried into the repo's token file with the same names and values: `space-2` (2px), `component-checkbox-size` (16px), `component-checkbox-iconSize` (12px), `component-statusDot-size` (8px), `component-groupHeader-height` (32px, the collapsible group header the All settings panel and the Check print report share).

Fork rules: before editing any file outside `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`, read `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md`; changes to OrcaSlicer-owned files must be small, product-neutral and additive, and the final report must list every upstream line changed. `AGENTS.md` has the build rules for the shared Mac: check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja` first, build with `-j4`, one build per build directory, never restart a build to change targets, start long builds with nohup in their own process group and watch the log. Never commit temporary working docs; leave them untracked in the worktree root.

TASK

Implement the Check print redesign on your branch, matching the four canvas boards.

1. Report panel. A native, fork-owned panel 360 DIP wide to the right of the preview inside `CheckPrintDialog` (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/StatusRow.cpp`), filled from `IWorkspace::slice_report` for the active plate with every section requested (`SliceReportRequest`: supports, seams, first_layer, islands, plus the project's region records so seams and support contacts are checked against marked faces). See `SliceReport` and its parts in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/Workspace.hpp` (around lines 1180 to 1291) and the adapter in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp`. Contents, top to bottom: a summary block (time, filament per extruder as grams and length, cost only when `has_cost`, filament changes only when more than zero); then sections in order of severity, Supports first whenever the slice generated any, else the most consequential finding first; each section is a collapsible group whose header row is the group-header token height with chevron, Body Small Bold title and a Label count at the right; each finding row is a status dot (red for a critical OrcaSlicer warning or a support contact with a region the person marked, amber for the rest, none when the row carries no severity), a Body Small message and a Label detail line under it with the object and the height or layer; a closing "Checked, nothing found: …" line that names every check that produced nothing. Pressing a finding selects the row (surface-selected fill), moves the camera to the object and the layer slider to the finding's height, and draws a small caption near the slider with the finding's name and "Layer N · Z mm". No buttons in the panel.

2. Two toggles in the window's header row (48 DIP: title "Check print", a Label with plate, object and printer, then the two checkboxes, then the close icon button). "Legend" drives `GCodeViewer::show_legend` (`src/slic3r/GUI/GCodeViewer.hpp` lines 338 to 340) and "Moves slider" drives `Preview::show_moves_sliders` (`src/slic3r/GUI/GUI_Preview.hpp` lines 156 to 157). Prefer routing them through the fork's `CanvasPresentationController` (`agent-docs/jusprin/architecture.md` already lists the Preview legend and sliders as presentation items that must be separately switchable and restored when the controller is destroyed) rather than calling OrcaSlicer directly from the dialog. The legend's view-type dropdown needs nothing: it is part of OrcaSlicer's legend.

3. Sliders in brand colour. Both of OrcaSlicer's preview sliders (the vertical layer slider and the horizontal moves slider) draw with the brand's action colour for the filled track, the end dot and the number-box text, a canvas-coloured ring handle, and the raised surface with the subtle elevation for the number boxes; the unfilled track uses border-strong. Find where OrcaSlicer sets those ImGui colours (its slider classes under `src/slic3r/GUI/`), add the smallest product-neutral seam (a colour set the fork can install, defaulting to OrcaSlicer's current colours), and install the brand colours from fork code through `ShellTheme`. Bed and legend colours stay OrcaSlicer's.

4. Tokens. Add the five tokens named above to the repo's token file with their guards, and draw every shared size in the panel from them (checkbox box and tick, status dot, group header height, the 2 DIP gap between a row's message and its detail line and inside the canvas caption). The panel width (360) and header height (48) may be one-off constants.

The branch builds (`cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo -- -j4`, after checking the machine is not already loaded); opening Check print on a sliced plate shows the panel with real `slice_report` data, the toggles show and hide the legend and moves slider, the sliders are brand-coloured, and selecting a finding moves the view; a shell-harness scenario covers the panel's contents for a plate with supports, one without, and one with nothing to flag, plus the toggles and the stale-close behaviour that already exists; a bitmap of the panel is rendered in the harness and checked by eye; Catch2 tests cover the section-ordering rule and the closing line; commits on the branch with messages a cold reader understands; your final message lists every line changed in an OrcaSlicer-owned file and what a future rebase must carry. description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
metadata:

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check
the new text is in resources/jusprin/agent/index.html before running live.

DISK (2026-10-10): building with `--config Release` instead of RelWithDebInfo made a fresh worktree build dir 859 MB instead of ~14 GB, needed no llvm-ar relink, and the shell harness ran normally from `tests/shell/Release/`. name: pkill-cmake-build-leaves-ninja
description: "Builds on this shared Mac — one at a time, capped -j, never restart to change targets; the 2026-10-21 run that stacked 4 builds / 56 clangs on 12 cores"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 63cd6f14-4717-4149-ae93-daff41a73f76
  modified: 2026-10-21T19:12:06.265Z
---

On 2026-10-21 Kenneth found 4 Release builds and 56 clang processes on 12 cores, all mine, in one worktree. Every ninja ran at its default -j (cores + 2), so 4 × 14 = 56. He pointed out that the orphaned processes were the smaller problem. The bigger one was that I put that many builds there at all.

What I did wrong, in order of weight:
1. I treated builds as free on a machine other sessions build on too. I never passed `-j`. I saw load 33, then 76, and started more builds anyway.
2. I restarted the build three times to change its target list or to slip in a small target. Each restart cost a full set of jobs. Waiting for the running build and adding targets afterwards cost nothing.
3. I went against the brief ("reuse the existing build; another session may be building") by configuring a fresh full-app build for an optional live check.
4. I blamed the slowness on "other sessions" without counting my own processes. That is the plausible-story-instead-of-checking failure from CLAUDE.md.
5. Mechanism: `pkill -f "cmake --build <dir>"` kills only the wrapper. Its `ninja -C <dir>` child keeps compiling as an orphan. I never checked that a stop had worked.

**Why:** the machine is shared. My extra jobs slow every other session, and two ninjas in one build dir can leave its records inconsistent.

**How to apply:**
- Before starting a build, check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja`. Cap jobs with `-- -j4` (fewer when load is above the core count).
- Decide the full target list once. Never restart a build to change it.
- Run one build per dir as its own process group (`set -m`, then kill with `kill -- -<pgid>`). After any stop, confirm with `pgrep -fl "ninja.*<dir>"`.
- Ask before a full-app build that the task did not require.

Related: [[background-bash-timeout-kills-builds]], [[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]], [[jusprin-worktree-build]].
---
name: render-widget-to-bitmap-for-visual-proof
description: Have the app draw its own widgets into a PNG for appearance evidence; behavioural assertions miss visual defects entirely, and screen capture is often unavailable.
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

For fork-owned wx controls, split painting from the paint event —
`paint(wxPaintEvent&)` builds the DC and delegates to
`draw(wxDC&, wxGraphicsContext&, wxSize)` — then add `snapshot()` that draws into
a `wxMemoryDC` over a `wxBitmap`. The shell harness writes those PNGs each run
(honour an env var like `JUSPRIN_ARTIFACT_DIR`; the harness deletes its temp data
dir at exit, so artifacts written there vanish before you can look).

Note `wxGraphicsContext::Create` has no generic `wxDC` overload — each caller
must build the context for its own concrete DC and pass it in.

**Why:** on the printer/spool chip slice, 267 green harness checks coexisted with
two real rendering defects, both found only by opening the image: a long-name
snapshot byte-identical to the normal one (the capture helper called `refresh()`
first, which re-read the store and undid the test's label — so the width
assertion compared a value to itself), and an inline detail overrunning the
trailing chevron under width pressure (measured width was correct; the overlap
was a painting error). Screen-control access was denied and `screencapture`
could not see the window, so in-app rendering was the only route.

**How to apply:** assert on raw pixel buffers (`wxImage::GetData` + `memcmp`) —
"light differs from dark", "long name differs from normal" — so a silently
reverted label fails instead of passing. Then still *open the image*; the
assertions prove difference, not correctness. See
[[live-test-built-app-on-mac]] and [[jusprin-chip-orca-seams]].

   - Web: `AgentUI/src/tokens.ts` writes the semantic colors as

   - Canvas: the Prepare canvas's tool strip (`Canvas/ViewportToolStrip`)
     paints with ImGui inside the GL frame, from the same `ShellTheme`. Its

     rasterized white and tinted with the token colour. ImGui 1.83 has no
     shadow primitive, so `elevation.medium` is approximated with stacked
     translucent rounded rectangles.
2. **Retained OrcaSlicer surfaces** are retinted through the color tables
   OrcaSlicer already routes its colors through, installed once per appearance
   mode by `JusPrin/Brand/BrandPalette.cpp` from the end of
   `GUI_App::init_label_colours`:
   - `StateColor::SetColorOverrides` maps OrcaSlicer's brand and surface
     literals (teal family, grays, whites, text grays) to semantic tokens before
     OrcaSlicer's own dark-mode remap runs. Every widget built on `StateColor`
     switches at once.
   - `BitmapCache::SetColorReplaces` rewrites the teal in the SVG icon set to
     the action color at load time, and the monochrome brand mark to the text
     color.
   - The canvas selection is OrcaSlicer's own, unretinted: its silhouette
     outline, which OrcaSlicer ships switched off and the shell switches on
     while it is installed, plus its white corner brackets. The brackets were
     briefly given the primary action color; on the dark build plate that
     measured 1.29:1 in light mode against white's 9:1, and with the outline
     carrying the selection the override was dropped on 2026-09-21, which
     left `Selection` untouched by the fork again.
   - The ImGui panels, the canvas selection rectangle, and the About dialog
     are left alone in source: those surfaces are slated to be hidden or
     replaced, so editing them would be divergence with no lasting value.
   - The mapping table in `BrandPalette.cpp` is the reviewed teal-to-purple
     decision. Extend it there; never add a purple literal to an OrcaSlicer file.
   - Widgets that paint the teal without going through `StateColor` (hyperlinks,
     the settings tab underline, notification accents, Bambu-only dialogs) are
     deliberately left teal; the cost of editing them in busy upstream files
     outweighs surfaces JusPrin rarely or never shows.
3. **Identity** comes from two data-only mechanisms:
   - `resources/jusprin/overlay/images/` holds the splash, About and horizontal
     lockups, monochrome mark, wizard watermark, and window icons under
     OrcaSlicer's own asset names. `Slic3r::var()` checks that directory
     first, so no logo call site is edited. See the README there.
   - `Brand/brand_catalogs.py` builds `resources/i18n/<lang>/<app key>.mo`
     from upstream's `.po` files with the product name substituted, plus an
     English catalog for the source strings, so every language reads "JusPrin"

   - The generic printer profiles' plate texture,
     `resources/profiles/Custom/orcaslicer_bed_texture.svg`, is overwritten
     with the JusPrin lockup; the file name stays because five profiles

184 agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md
# Fork stewardship

**Status:** Required discipline for every change to an upstream-owned file on `jusprin-newui`.

JusPrin is a long-lived fork. Every line it changes in an OrcaSlicer-owned file is a line it re-resolves at every rebase, forever, by a person who was not there when the line was written. The rules below exist to keep that permanent cost small and, where it cannot be small, to keep it visible.

One question generates all of them: **after this change, what does the fork own?**

- Owning *product policy* is safe. It is ours, upstream will never write it, and it lives in our files.
- Owning a *small neutral seam* is acceptable. It is the kind of thing upstream might plausibly have written itself, so it survives refactors and could be contributed back.
- Owning *upstream's behavior* is the expensive kind. It commits us to re-deriving upstream's intent forever, and the day we take ownership is usually the day the behavior quietly diverges.

Two mechanical facts drive everything else. Git merges text, not meaning: it conflicts when two sides touch the same or adjacent lines, and it stays silent when they touch different lines even if the result is nonsense. And a conflict is a *stop* — a human is forced to look — while silent divergence is unbounded and invisible. Conflicts are therefore not the enemy. Unnoticed drift is, and conflicts that resolve wrongly are.

## The ten principles

### 1. Conflict probability is about where you write, not how much

**Rule.** Place fork edits where upstream rarely writes, and keep the number of distinct sites low.

**Mechanism.** Risk is roughly *how often upstream edits this region* times *how much of the region you occupy*, summed over every place you touched. Each site is an independent draw. New files have probability zero, so their size is free; one line inside a function upstream is actively reworking is expensive.

**The test.** How many separate places does this change touch, and how busy is each one? Would one seam deliver the same capability?

**Violation.** Delivering a single capability through a dozen scattered notification lines across several upstream files, when one funnel that every path already passes through would have carried them.

### 2. A clean merge is not a safe merge

**Rule.** Prefer edits that are locally correct over edits that participate in upstream's control flow.

**Mechanism.** Git merges text. If your edit's correctness depends on the code around it — an ordering, a guard, an early return, an invariant nobody wrote down — upstream can restructure the surroundings, the merge succeeds, and your edit now runs under assumptions that no longer hold, with no signal at all.

**The test.** If upstream restructures the code around this hunk, do I get a conflict or silence? If silence, would any test catch it?

**Violation.** Moving a member out of a constructor's initializer list because a callback can fire mid-construction. Nothing in upstream's code records that invariant, so a future cleanup restores the old form with no conflict and no error.

### 3. Add to upstream's code; do not revise it

**Rule.** Append, insert, and call. Do not rewrite upstream functions or change their signatures.

**Mechanism.** An additive hook fails gracefully: when it conflicts, the resolution is "keep both," and anyone can do that correctly. A rewritten function fails badly: every future upstream change to it is a conflict whose resolution requires re-deriving two intents at once, in code no longer shared with upstream. Rewriting subtle logic also tends to change it, and you find out later.

**The test.** Does upstream's line survive my change? If I deleted or replaced one, why could I not have added next to it?

**Violation.** Replacing OrcaSlicer's undo and redo implementations with fork-owned equivalents in order to learn whether the history position moved. Re-expressing the vendor-specific snapshot walk silently dropped one of its branches. An additive helper that reports the result, leaving upstream's functions untouched, would have answered the same question.

### 4. Own the policy; borrow the mechanism

**Rule.** No product name, color, dimension, or product-specific decision in an upstream-owned file. Upstream files may gain small neutral capabilities; the policy that uses them lives in fork-owned code.

**Mechanism.** Product specifics in upstream files are permanent divergence: they can never be upstreamed and never dropped, so they must be re-resolved forever. A neutral capability — a flag, a getter/setter pair, an event — reads like something upstream could have written, which is exactly why it survives refactors.

**The test.** Would this addition look reasonable in an upstream pull request, with no explanation of our product?

**Violation.** A product-named enum value inside a rendering class, or product decisions embedded in an upstream mouse handler. The fix is a neutral options struct plus a fork-owned controller that applies our policy.

### 5. One seam beats many touch points

**Rule.** Find the single place every path already passes through, and put the fork's line there.

**Mechanism.** Each touch point is an independent conflict draw and an independent thing a future resolver must understand. Collapsing many small recurring costs into one is worth some indirection.

**The test.** Do all the paths I am hooking already converge somewhere downstream? Is there one function that runs exactly when the thing I care about has happened?

**Violation.** Publishing a history-changed event from undo, from redo, and from both history-navigation entry points, when all four funnel through a single update function that runs only on a successful move.

### 6. One shared implementation is worth a guaranteed conflict

**Rule.** When the alternative is two copies of the same behavior, keep the shared path and accept that it will conflict.

**Mechanism.** A conflict is a stop; drift between two copies is silent and unbounded. Trading an invisible risk for a visible, small, recurring one is a good trade.

**The test.** Where did the logic I removed actually go? A move has one implementation; only a duplication risks divergence. If I wrote new behavior beside an existing upstream path rather than calling it, upstream's future improvements will never reach our users.

**Violation.** Writing a second object-duplication routine next to OrcaSlicer's clipboard path and pointing an existing dialog at it. Reusing the existing path — extending it where it was too narrow — keeps one implementation.

### 7. Unavoidable conflicts must be easy to resolve correctly

**Rule.** When you must delete or relocate an upstream line, say at the site what moved, where it went, and what a future rebase must carry across.

**Mechanism.** The real cost of a conflict is not the stop; it is the chance of resolving it wrongly. Appending near an upstream line yields a conflict whose obvious resolution — keep both — is right. Deleting an upstream line yields a conflict whose obvious resolution — take mine, the logic moved — silently discards whatever upstream did to that line in the meantime.

**The test.** Six months from now, is the natural resolution of the conflict I am creating the correct one? If not, what does the resolver need to read to get it right, and is that text next to the conflict?

**Violation.** Removing an upstream snapshot label that upstream later localized. Git stops for a human, but the intent-faithful resolution throws the translation away, and nothing at the site says otherwise.

### 8. Do not diverge where you gain nothing; converge where upstream already went

**Rule.** No gratuitous formatting, reordering, or whitespace differences. Before reverting a cosmetic difference, compare against current upstream — it may have made the same change.

**Mechanism.** Every valueless difference is a conflict site that buys nothing. And if upstream has independently arrived at your version, "fixing" it back creates divergence rather than removing it. Adopting a change upstream has already made converges the two trees early and makes the eventual conflict resolve itself.

**The test.** Does this difference carry meaning? Has upstream already made it?

**Violation.** Consuming a shared blank line in a list of build subdirectories, where upstream also appends entries.

### 9. Verify the risk claim instead of reasoning about it

**Rule.** Before asserting that a change is or is not rebase-risky, check it. Three checks, each one command: does git actually conflict there; has upstream already converged on the same change; is the change a move or a duplication.

**Mechanism.** A coherent story about fork risk is not a true one, and every one of these is cheaper to check than to argue about. Reasoning alone reliably produces confident, wrong claims — that a lost change is "silent" when git stops for it, that a move is a "duplication," that a cosmetic difference is gratuitous when upstream shares it.

**The test.** Did I run the simulation, or am I describing what I expect it to say?

**Violation.** A report that lists which files are rebase-sensitive and calls the change narrow, without having run the merge simulation that would have found two lossy resolutions waiting in it.

### 10. Pull direction dominates every local edit

**Rule.** Replay the fork's own commits onto upstream. Never merge upstream in, and never rebase the whole branch.

**Mechanism.** The fork's own footprint is small; the inherited release-branch history is not. Merging upstream in makes the conflict surface the entire divergence between the release branch and upstream's development line — none of it ours. Rebasing only our commits discards that inherited history by taking upstream's version of every file we never touched.

**The test.** Am I replaying our commits onto upstream, or bringing upstream into ours?

**Violation.** `git merge upstream/main`, which produces a conflict list dominated by vendor profiles, translations, and CI files that JusPrin has never edited.

## Before you finish

A change that touches upstream-owned files is not done until this is recorded in the handback or pull request:

1. **The rebase simulation and its result.** Run it against current upstream and name both endpoint commits — measurements are not reproducible otherwise.

   ```bash
   git merge-tree --write-tree --merge-base=<fork base> upstream/main HEAD
   ```

   For each conflicted file, state whether the natural resolution is correct or lossy. A lossy one is a defect to fix now, not a note for later.

2. **An account of every upstream line deleted or rewritten.** Where the logic went, and why an additive form was not possible.

3. **A statement of what the fork now owns.** Policy, a neutral seam, or upstream behavior. The third needs an explicit justification.

An automatic merge is evidence about today's text. It is not proof that a future rebase will merge, and never proof that the merged result behaves correctly. After every upstream update, run the focused contract tests, the full native build, the real multi-plate workflow, native gizmo input, and the stock-behavior regression checks.

## This fork's terrain

Facts specific to OrcaSlicer, worth knowing before choosing where to put a seam. They change over time; re-measure rather than trusting these.

`Plater.cpp` is by far the busiest file the fork touches, followed by the central `src/slic3r/CMakeLists.txt`, `GLCanvas3D.cpp`, and `PartPlate.cpp`. `GLToolbar` and `GLGizmosManager` are quiet. File-level churn is only a first approximation: some functions inside `Plater.cpp` have not been touched upstream in the entire life of this fork, and a seam there is far cheaper than the file's overall rate suggests. Measure the function, not just the file.

Some native state is shared rather than owned by one object. OrcaSlicer's collapse toolbar belongs to `Plater` and is used by both the Prepare and Preview canvases, so a per-canvas guard cannot save and restore it correctly. Shared state needs one owner at the shared lifetime boundary, and exact restoration needs a getter as well as a setter.

`MainFrame`'s Notebook is cheaper to wrap than to dismantle. Dozens of
upstream predicates — menu and shortcut enabling, `can_delete`, slice status
updates, undo/redo gating — key off `m_tabpanel->GetSelection()`, so removing
or reparenting the Prepare/Preview pages breaks them with no conflict and no
error. A shell gets a tabless full-window layout for free instead: hide the
strip via the public `GetBtnsListCtrl()` (wxBookCtrlBase gives a hidden
controller zero size, so pages fill the client area), and the stock slice and
print side buttons disappear with it because `ButtonsListCtrl` reparents them
into the strip at construction. The Phase 1 production shell reached a
19-added-line upstream footprint this way where the POC's reparenting shell
needed edits across eight upstream files.

The same measurement gives the rule for every fork-owned screen that comes
after the shell. OrcaSlicer's surfaces (the stock homepage, Prepare, Preview,
Monitor, the settings tabs) stay inside the Notebook, because their
correctness depends on it. Fork-owned surfaces (the header, the Agent pane,
Home, and whatever follows) live outside it, as siblings of the Notebook in a
fork-owned sizer, shown and hidden by the shell. The shell *reads* the
Notebook's selection to decide what to show and *never edits its page list*:
no `RemovePage`, `InsertPage`, or reparenting of a stock page. Removing or
replacing a page hands the fork the meaning of that index. Upstream keeps
addressing it by number — `tpHome` as a dialog parent, the target of
`EVT_LOAD_URL`, the tab `post_init` returns to — and every one of those lands
on the fork's widget with no conflict and no error. If a fork surface truly
must be a page, append it last, where no upstream code addresses it.

Navigation between screens stays a Notebook selection change even when the
screen being left is fork-owned. Menu and shortcut enabling, undo and redo
availability, and slice-status updates all read `GetSelection()`, so the
selection must remain the one record of which OrcaSlicer surface is active.
Showing Prepare any other way leaves those predicates answering for the wrong
page, silently.

Some stock behavior is already exposed as an event idiom rather than a
function. Upstream itself drives plate slicing from two places with the same
sequence — the slice button and the Cmd+R shortcut both run
`plater->update(true, true)`, post `EVT_GLTOOLBAR_SLICE_PLATE` to the Plater,
and select the Preview tab — so fork code may repeat that short dispatch
without violating the shared-implementation rule; the behavior itself stays
owned by Plater's event handler.

Historical measurements and the incidents behind several of these rules are in the [OrcaSlicer integration guide](orca-integration-guide.md) and, for the spike era, in the [POC reference](poc-reference.md).

The Klipper/Moonraker simulator lives on `jusprin-newui-fakeprinter` under
`tests/printer_sim/` and covers print-host printers. Do not add a Bambu network
fake unless asked.

This file is the operator guide for humans and AI agents.

## What success looks like

- Log: `switch_printer_agent: printer agent switched to jusprin-fake-bambu`
- Log: `set_selected_machine=FAKE001` and later `FakeBambuAgent: connected FAKE001`
- Printer chip shows `Bambu Lab A1 mini · 0.4` (nickname and nozzle only)
- Click the **printer** half of that chip. The **first menu row** is Idle,
  Printing, or Offline. Those words are never on the chip itself.

If the log says `moonraker` or `orca`, the fake is not in the path. Stop and
fix the preset; do not patch UI gates.

## Turn it on

Quit JusPrin first. The app rewrites `JusPrin2.conf` on exit.

`JusPrin2.conf` is JSON. Under the scratch datadir:

```json
"jusprin": { "fake_printer": true }
```

JSON `true` is what the app stores; `get("jusprin", "fake_printer")` reads as
the string `"true"`. An INI `[jusprin]` block is ignored.

Keep a **Bambu Lab printer** selected: a real system preset, typically
`Bambu Lab A1 mini 0.4 nozzle`, or a named printer that inherits one.
`is_bbl_vendor()` must be true; it reads the inherited `printer_model`, so
either works. An embedded 3mf preset named
`Bambu Lab A1 mini 0.4 nozzle(Tape_4_3MF.3mf)` is not enough; the agent stays
`orca`.

**Add a printer…** in the printer menu installs the system preset and saves it
as a named printer (a user profile such as `Bambu Lab A1 mini`), which is what
Home lists. Alternatively copy `Resources/profiles/BBL` into
`<datadir>/system/` and add the A1 mini model to the `models` array in
`JusPrin2.conf`, then select the system preset. Opening
`~/Downloads/Tape_4_3MF.3mf` only helps after that vendor is installed.

Launch a **scratch** `--datadir`. Do not point fake mode at the everyday
config. Set `"single_instance": false` in the `app` object if another JusPrin
is already running. Do not pass `--no-single-instance`; Boost rejects it.

The fake emulates printer type `N1` (A1 mini). Select Machine lists it as
**JusPrin Fake A1 mini (LAN)**.

## Drive state

Write `<datadir>/jusprin/fake_printer.json` (create `jusprin/` if needed). The
fake rereads it about once a second.

```json
{"state":"printing","progress":0.4,"nozzle":210,"bed":60,"offline":false}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `state` | `idle`, `heating`/`prepare`, `printing`/`running`, `pause`, `finished`, `failed` |
| `progress` | 0–1, mapped to `mc_percent` |
| `nozzle`, `bed` | °C |
| `offline` | `true` stops `push_status`; after ~30 s the menu first row is Offline |
| `spools` | loaded AMS spools; see below. Absent leaves whatever was last set |

No `spools` (or an empty array) reports no AMS at all, same as before this
field existed. A non-empty array reports one AMS unit (id `"0"`) with one
tray per spool, up to 4:

```json
{"spools": [{"subBrands": "PLA Matte", "trayType": "PLA", "colour": "5F7D4FFF"}]}
```

`subBrands` is what `PrinterDiscovery.cpp` reads back as the spool's name
when set (ahead of `trayType`), so it is the field worth setting for a
saved/network-printer card or receipt to show something. `trayType` is the
spool's material (Home's Loaded row names it); the fake sends it beside a
`tray_info_idx`, since upstream ignores a type that arrives without one.
`filamentId` sets that id (`"GFA01"` is Bambu PLA Matte); left out, the
id is empty, and Orca's filament sync skips the tray. `colour` is optional: a spool without it reports no colour, and Home
draws no swatch for it.

Delete the file, or set `"offline": false` and `"state":"idle"`, to return to Idle.

## Print

Slice, then Print (or Cmd+Shift+G on macOS). Send completes without a printer.
The log records `FakeBambuAgent: start_local_print file=...`.

If the control file is present, that file wins: send still succeeds, but the
menu stays on the file's state. Remove the file if you want the canned printing
scenario after send.

## Isolate a running app (agents)

Another JusPrin may already be open. Do not send keys or clicks to it.

On macOS both processes are often named `OrcaSlicer`. Target by unix pid or by
a unique `CFBundleIdentifier` on a ditto'd `.app` (then ad-hoc `codesign`).
`osascript` `unix id` filters can match the wrong process; prefer
`AXUIElementCreateApplication(pid)` or the unique bundle id.

Keyboard events posted to the pid work while the Mac is locked; mouse events
posted that way do not. Menus only open when that app is frontmost. The printer
half of the chip is a wx control (`SetName("Printer")`) and often has no AX
title; click by coordinates after a screenshot, or use the documented shortcut
for Print.

Logs: `<datadir>/log/debug_*.log`. This machine's default `grep` may be ugrep;
use `/usr/bin/grep -a` on app logs.

## Unit tests

`jusprin_fake_bambu_tests` (Catch2, GUI build). They cover announce JSON,
control-file parsing, and agent id. They do not start the heartbeat unless the
test sets `set_queue_on_main_fn`.

## Agent id

Registered as `jusprin-fake-bambu`. `GUI_App::switch_printer_agent` uses that
id in place of `bbl` when fake mode is on. No other upstream file is involved.

I've implemented the Check print redesign as four commits on `claude/check-print-report-82ed92`, 570a723ad0..e5cded31f9, on top of jusprin-newui bed54fd8fe. Nothing is pushed or merged, and I haven't looked at it in the live app yet.

The worktree had been created from `main`, which has none of the Check print code, so I first pointed the branch at jusprin-newui. The branch had no commits of its own, so nothing was lost.

**What's built**
- **Report panel:** 360 DIP wide, filled from `slice_report` with every section and the project's region records. Supports come first whenever any were generated, then sections by severity, then a closing "Checked, nothing found" line. Pressing a finding moves the camera, the layer slider and a caption on the canvas. On close, the camera goes back to where it was before a finding moved it, because Prepare shares that camera.
- **Header:** 48 DIP, with the title, what was sliced, the Legend and Moves slider switches (both off at every opening, not remembered), and Close.
- **Sliders:** OrcaSlicer's layer and moves sliders are drawn in the brand colours. The legend and bed keep OrcaSlicer's colours.
- **Tokens:** three of the five already existed in the token file under the repo's own names. I added the 2 DIP half step as `dimension.space["0.5"]` and `component.groupHeader.height` = 32, with guards.

**Results**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Full build, `-j4` | passes |
| Report model tests (Catch2) | 50 assertions pass |
| Token and theme tests | pass; both new guards fail when given a wrong value |
| New `--check-print` harness run | 150 checks pass |
| Default, `--print-issues`, `--print-issue-readers` runs | 566, 484 and 253 checks pass |

I looked at the panel, switch and canvas pictures by eye. The new harness run covers a plate with nothing to flag, one with supports, and one without supports that has a slab printed in the air, plus both switches and the self-close when the slice goes stale.

**Bug found and fixed:** OrcaSlicer uses one ImGui context for every canvas but resets its size only when a canvas resizes. The new layout made the preview smaller than the Prepare canvas, so the sliders and caption were drawn about one header-height too high. The old window only worked because its preview was exactly the Prepare canvas's size. I reproduced it in the harness, fixed it, and showed the new check fails without the fix.

**Choices I made that are Kenneth's to confirm**
- **G-code listing:** OrcaSlicer's G-code listing is an app-wide setting that opened over the canvas whenever a finding moved the layer slider. It now shows only while the Moves slider switch is on, and the setting is restored on close.
- **Toggles not remembered:** both switches start off every time, because that was the simplest choice.
- **Order rule over board 1:** I followed the brief's rule, so sections go strictly by severity. Board 1 shows Seams (amber) above a red OrcaSlicer warning.
- **Text and colour details:**
  - Toggle labels use Body Small as the board shows, though the checkbox token names Body.
  - Detail lines show one height per finding, because `slice_report` has no height ranges.
  - OrcaSlicer's layer-mode button stays teal, and its view cube and round canvas buttons are untouched.

**One mistake:** while restarting a harness run I used a `pkill` pattern that would also match other worktrees' harness processes. No other harness was running afterwards, but another session's run may have been stopped.

**Lines changed in OrcaSlicer-owned files**
- **`GLCanvas3D.cpp`:** 3 added lines in `render()` after `camera.apply_viewport()`, setting the ImGui display size every frame.
- **`IMSlider.hpp`:** 28 added lines: `#include <optional>`, the `Colors` struct, `SetColorOverrides`, `show`/`is_shown`, and the `m_shown` member.
- **`IMSlider.cpp`:**
  - 13 added lines:
    - the override storage and setter;
    - two lines drawing the lower end dot;
    - early returns in `render()` and `on_mouse_wheel()`;
    - one comment.
  - 23 rewritten lines:
    - 20 colour locals across `draw_background_and_groove`, `horizontal_slider` and `vertical_slider`;
    - the label hover border;
    - the value-text colour;
    - the wheel handler's window check, which now needs only its own slider's window.

**What a rebase must carry:** each rewritten colour line has the form `s_color_overrides ? s_color_overrides->X : <upstream's expression>`. If upstream changes one, keep upstream's new expression and put the ternary back around it. Replaying these commits onto upstream main 14a1aa333b auto-merges all three files.

## Kenneth's findings 1–7

### 1. Blank white rounded pill at the top-left of the preview canvas — reproduced, identified
Steps: slice, open Check print. Observed on every opening (`evidence/01-dialog-initial-state.jpg`, `09-c-key-hides-gcode-listing.jpg`, harness `check-print-canvas-default.png`).
It is OrcaSlicer's plate-selector strip (`GLCanvas3D::_render_imgui_select_plate_toolbar`, called from `_render_overlays` at `src/slic3r/GUI/GLCanvas3D.cpp:8431`). `Preview::init` enables it for every editor preview (`src/slic3r/GUI/GUI_Preview.cpp:276`, `enable_select_plate_toolbar(true)`), and `Plater::create_preview` (Plater.cpp:17253) builds the dialog's preview through the same constructor. Why it is blank: hypothesis — the thumbnail textures are generated for the Plater's own preview canvas, never for this second canvas, so the item draws its frame with no image. Hidden by `set_legacy_overlays_hidden(true)` (GLCanvas3D.cpp:2151 skips `_render_overlays`).

### 2. 3D navigator cube at the bottom-left — reproduced
`_render_3d_navigator()` at GLCanvas3D.cpp:8463, inside `_render_overlays`. Same evidence as 1. Hidden by the same flag.

### 3. Canvas toolbar (menu and magnifier buttons) at the bottom-left — reproduced
`_render_canvas_toolbar()` at GLCanvas3D.cpp:8465, inside `_render_overlays`. Same evidence. Hidden by the same flag.

### 4. "Assemble-view" layers icon at the bottom-right — reproduced, but it is not the assemble toolbar
`Preview::init` disables the assemble toolbar (`GUI_Preview.cpp:280`, `enable_assemble_view_toolbar(false)`). The icon is the layer slider's own "show one layer" button: `IMSlider::render` draws it at the canvas's bottom-right corner (`src/slic3r/GUI/IMSlider.cpp:1273-1285`, `ImGui::ImageButton3(normal_id, hover_id, ONE_LAYER_BUTTON_SIZE)`), from textures loaded at IMSlider.cpp:155-162: `resources/images/one_layer_off.svg` (fills `#009688` teal and `#fff`), plus `one_layer_on`, `_hover` and `_dark` variants. It is drawn from `GCodeViewer::render_slider`, not from `_render_overlays`, so hiding the legacy overlays keeps it, which is what Kenneth wants.
Brand colour at no upstream cost: partly. The fork's resource overlay (`resources/jusprin/overlay/images`, installed by `BrandPalette.cpp:124`) hooks `Slic3r::var()`, but IMSlider builds the path from `Slic3r::resources_dir() + "/images/..."` directly (IMSlider.cpp:155), so an overlay SVG would not apply. Either edit the eight SVGs in `resources/images` in place (resource files, no code) or change those eight lines to `var(...)`.
Evidence: `evidence/01`, `09`, harness `check-print-canvas-default.png` (green stack bottom-right).

### 5. "Untitled" and "01" on the bed — reproduced; hiding legacy overlays would not remove the number
Visible once the camera shows the plate (`evidence/06-finding-selected-marker-box-shown.jpg`, `09`, `20`). The plate number is drawn by `PartPlate::render_only_numbers(bottom)` at `src/slic3r/GUI/PartPlate.cpp:3394-3397`, which runs whether or not `only_body` is set (the flag the legacy-overlay switch turns on, GLCanvas3D.cpp:2062). The name texture goes through `render_icons(bottom, only_body, hover_id)` (PartPlate.cpp:3394); whether `only_body` suppresses it there is unverified. Note that Prepare's canvas, which has the controller attached, shows both labels too (`evidence/00a-prepare-canvas-before-slicing-shows-plate-name-and-number.jpg`), so this is not a difference between the two canvases.

Verification of the hypothesis for 1–5: `PreviewPresentationController` (CanvasPresentationController.cpp:84-103) never calls `set_legacy_overlays_hidden`; `CanvasPresentationController::attach` does (line 22-23) and Prepare attaches it at ShellController.cpp:609. So 1, 2 and 3 are explained by that one missing call; 5 is not (see above); 4 is unaffected by it.

### 6. OrcaSlicer's G-code listing is drawn over the bed and the Legend switch does not hide it — reproduced exactly
Steps: open the window (listing present, `evidence/01-dialog-initial-state.jpg`); Legend on (listing stays, moves down below the legend, `02-dialog-legend-on.jpg`); Legend off (listing back where it was, `03-dialog-legend-off-again.jpg`).
Verified in code: the listing is `GCodeViewer::SequentialView::GCodeWindow::render`, called from `SequentialView::render` whenever a path exists (GCodeViewer.cpp:972), with no legend condition; its own gate is `wxGetApp().show_gcode_window()` (GCodeViewer.cpp:810), which is `GUI_App::m_show_gcode_window{true}` (GUI_App.hpp:337) read from the app config key `show_gcode_window` (GUI_App.cpp:910). It is not inside `_render_overlays`, so the legacy flag would not touch it either. Proof: pressing C (GLCanvas3D.cpp:3549 → `toggle_show_gcode_window`) with the canvas focused removed it (`evidence/09-c-key-hides-gcode-listing.jpg`). The legend's `</>` button calls the same toggle (GCodeViewer.cpp:3470); not pressed (needs the mouse). The View menu's "Show G-code Window" item is disabled while the modal is open.
Side effect, see 16: C persists the change to the user's app config.

### 7. Tool-position box at the bottom centre, over the moves slider, also with Legend off — reproduced
Steps: open, select the first finding (layer slider goes to layer 1), box appears "X 5.390 Y 249.130 Z 0.200 / Speed: 105 Bottom surface" over the left end of the moves slider (`evidence/06-finding-selected-marker-box-shown.jpg`); Legend on (`07`), Legend off (`08-legend-off-marker-box-still-shown.jpg`): the box stays.
Verified in code: `SequentialView::render` draws `marker.render_position_window` when `m_show_marker` (GCodeViewer.cpp:959), positioned at 0.5·width, bottom edge (GCodeViewer.cpp:335). `m_show_marker` is set in `GCodeViewer::render` at line 1596 when the visible range's end differs from the full range's end, and it is sticky until the next `load_toolpaths` (line 1388). So it appears when the moves slider is anywhere but the end, and also after `show_finding` moves the layer slider down (the layer change shortens the range). One quirk seen: after a keyboard move of the slider the box only appears on the next frame, because line 1596 is evaluated before `render_slider` applies the slider at line 1639 (`evidence/04`, `05` show the moved slider with no box; lldb read `m_show_marker=false` with visible range end 347340 vs full 347343; the box came with the next frame).

## New findings

### 8. Keyboard focus is trapped in the preview canvas: Tab never reaches Legend, Close or the report
Steps: open the window; press Tab (any number of times). `wxWindow::FindFocus()` read in lldb stays on the `GLCanvas` after Tab; with the report panel focused it stays on `Print report` after three Tabs. Only Escape works from the keyboard.
Verified: the canvas turns Tab into `EVT_GLCANVAS_TAB` (GLCanvas3D.cpp:3747-3750), which only the Plater's own canvases bind (Plater.cpp:5185 and 5255); the dialog's preview has no handler, so Tab is swallowed. The report panel is created with `wxWANTS_CHARS` (CheckPrintReportPanel.cpp:133), which on macOS also keeps Tab from traversing. Expected: Tab order canvas → Legend → Close → report (design-system keyboard rules); the focus ring code exists on CheckToggle and the Quiet button but can never be reached.

### 9. Selecting a row from the keyboard does not scroll it into view
Steps: a report taller than the panel (22 first-layer rows, content 1302 px in a 911 px panel); focus the panel; press Up (selects the last row). Observed: `m_selected = {0,21}`, `m_scroll = 0`, caption and camera update, but the highlighted row is below the fold (`evidence/16-keyboard-selected-last-row-not-scrolled-into-view.jpg`; after setting `m_scroll` to the bottom it is there, `17-long-report-scrolled-to-bottom.jpg`). Verified: `CheckPrintReportPanel::select` (CheckPrintReportPanel.cpp:~170) and `on_key` never adjust `m_scroll`.

### 10. A long report gives no sign that it scrolls
Same state as 9: rows run off the bottom edge with no scrollbar, fade or cut row (`evidence/15-long-report-22-rows-no-scroll-indicator.jpg`). The wheel scrolls it (code; not driven here). The boards do not show the overflow case, so this may be a design gap rather than a code bug.

### 11. The finding caption sits on top of OrcaSlicer's overlays
With Legend off the caption is drawn over the G-code listing's first lines (`evidence/06`); with Legend on it covers the legend's view-type dropdown row (`evidence/07-legend-on-with-marker-caption-overlaps-legend.jpg`). `draw_caption` places it at canvas width − 76 DIP, top = space_3 (CheckPrintDialog.cpp, `kCaptionRightInsetDip`), which is the corner the legend and G-code window occupy, and it calls `BringWindowToDisplayFront` so it always wins. The board (`check-print-03`) assumes that corner is empty. Goes away for the listing once 6 is fixed; the legend-on overlap remains.

### 12. The window opens with whatever camera Prepare had, not fitted to the plate
Steps: zoom Prepare in (any way; here OrcaSlicer's preview had been zoomed by Cmd+R), open Check print. Observed: the first opening showed a corner of the headband (`evidence/01`), the second plate opened as a solid red wall (`12-second-plate-opens-with-prepare-camera-zoomed-in.jpg`), the cubes plate opened on empty grey (`15`). Verified: the constructor sets up the preview and report but never calls `zoom_to_gcode`/`zoom_to_bed`; the camera is the Plater's shared one (`m_plater.get_camera()`), and only `show_finding` moves it. Board `check-print-01` shows the whole plate on opening. Closing does put Prepare's camera back (checked after a finding moved it, `evidence/00`-style main-window screenshot matched the pre-open view).

### 13. No minimum window size; at 900×600 OrcaSlicer's overlays pile on each other
`GetMinSize()` is (−1,−1) and the dialog has `wxRESIZE_BORDER`. At 900×600 the panel keeps 360 and the preview is 540 wide: the moves slider's left end sits under the magnifier button and the navigator overlaps the listing (`evidence/13-window-900x600-overlays-collide.jpg`). At 1700×1050 the layout is fine (`14-window-1700x1050.jpg`); the panel width stays, nothing clipped.

### 14. Dark mode: the Close button draws a lighter box behind the X
Steps: dark mode (set per app with `defaults write io.jusprin.check-print-test AppleInterfaceStyle Dark`; `mac_dark_mode()` reads that key, MacDarkMode.mm:28), open Check print. Observed: a grey square behind the X at the header's right (`evidence/19-dark-mode-dialog-crossing-paths-case.jpg`, `20`); in light mode nothing. Verified: `HeaderButton::draw` clears and fills a `HeaderStyle::Quiet` button with `surface_canvas` (HeaderControls.cpp:~406 and the `fill` expression that follows), while `build_header` paints the header `surface_raised` (CheckPrintDialog.cpp); the two tokens coincide in light and differ in dark. Everything else in dark reads correctly: panel, summary, pink (action) sliders, value boxes with pink text on dark, caption.

### 15. A stale hover tooltip ("40m22s") and hover ring sit on the layer slider with no pointer in the window
Seen at the top of the layer slider from the first frame, and it stayed there after the handle moved to the bottom (`evidence/02`, `03`, `04`, `06`). lldb: `ImGui::GetIO().MousePos = (823,102)` with `DisplaySize = (835,911)` while the real pointer was on another display. Hypothesis: the single ImGui context keeps the last mouse position fed by another canvas (commit 570a723ad0 gives each canvas its own size per frame, not its own mouse state), so the dialog's slider sees a hover at a point it never received a mouse-move for and draws the layer-time tooltip (IMSlider.cpp:873-874).

### 16. Pressing C inside Check print changes and persists the app-wide "Show G-code Window" preference
Steps: canvas focused, press C. Observed: listing hidden, and `datadir/JusPrin2.conf` now has `"show_gcode_window": false` (checked with grep; pressing C again set it back to true). Verified: GLCanvas3D.cpp:3549 → `GUI_App::toggle_show_gcode_window` writes `app_config->set_bool` (GUI_App.cpp:716-719). A modal review window silently edits a global preference; the same is true of the legend's `</>` button.

### 17. The panel follows the active plate; the header shows the stale-close path works from outside the app
Not bugs, recorded as verified behaviour: with three plates the window opened on the active one each time ("Second plate · towel-box-bottom.stl …", `evidence/12`; "Cubes · towel-box-spring.stl and 21 more …", `15`; "Plate 1 · arrow headband.STL and 1 more …", `19`). A process setting changed through the MCP endpoint while the window was open closed it within 2 s. Escape closes from the canvas and from the panel. The summary matched OrcaSlicer's legend totals (legend 40m22s / 5.74 m / 18.22 g / 0.46 against panel 40 min / 5.7 m / 18 g / $0.46; `slice_report` printTimeSeconds 2422). Section order held in every case seen: harness cp_b Supports first (`harness-capture/check-print-supports.png`), cp_c OrcaSlicer warnings (red) → Unsupported islands (amber) → First layer (`check-print-island.png`), live Crossing paths (red) → First layer (`19`); each closing line named exactly the checks not shown. Five openings across two instances with re-slices and plate changes in between: no crash, no assertion; the only `[error]` lines in `datadir/log/debug_*.log` are OrcaSlicer's own (`call_process:got cancelled exception` from cancelled slices, `gcode path conflicts found`).

## Deviations from the boards (not filed as bugs)
- Boards 01/02 have a second header checkbox, "Moves slider", off at opening; the build has only Legend and always shows the moves slider (the commit message says this was deliberate; the brief says Kenneth is undecided).
- The caption title is drawn in ImGui's regular font; board 03 uses `label-bold` for the title and `label` for "Layer N · Z mm".
- The Supports section count reads "43 layers"; the board writes "2 objects · 96 layers".

## Side observations outside Check print (lower confidence, from the route used)
- Cmd+R (OrcaSlicer's slice accelerator) switches the main window to OrcaSlicer's Preview tab with its legend, listing and toolbars (`evidence/00-main-window-after-cmd-r-slice.jpg`, `18`). Probably pre-existing; not checked against `jusprin-newui`.
- The print-actions popup stayed open with stale rows while the slice finished underneath ("Slice all plates" as the only row while the primary button already read "Print plate 2", `evidence/11-two-plates-menu-lacks-check-print.jpg`); a posted Escape did not close it. My keys are posted to the pid rather than typed, so treat this as a lead, not a repro.

## Not reproduced / not tested, and why
- Mouse-driven checks: dragging either slider, wheel over the layer slider, hover highlight on rows, clicking a row or a section header, the Close button, the legend's `</>` and collapse buttons. No pointer route (see the top). Keyboard and lldb equivalents were used instead; the harness covers `panel.select`, `toggle_section` and the switch.
- Two filaments: the project has one filament slot, `printer_setup_preview` refused a second preset ("This project has 1 filament slots"), and there is no keyboard route to add a slot. The harness has no two-filament case either. The per-extruder rows and the "Changes" row in `draw_summary` are untested.
- Supports section live: only the harness (cp_b PASS, bitmap above); no live opening with generated supports.
- Undo/redo keys while the window is modal: not tried.
- Opening on a small main window: the dialog takes the plater's client size at opening; I resized the dialog itself instead (13).
- Wrapping and ellipsis of long object names: the harness caption shows the ellipsis ("20mmbox-LF.stl · 400 mm² o…", `check-print-canvas-default.png`) and the panel wrapped the crossing-paths message over two lines (`19`); no object name long enough to ellipsize in a row was available.

content.text:
I've fixed everything from the live-test report in fork code and committed it on `claude/check-print-report-82ed92` as two new commits, 53471f582b and 713f02b03c, on top of e9e8887e6c. I added them as new commits rather than squashing, so no history was rewritten and no approval was needed. Nothing is pushed.

The upstream footprint is unchanged: the 16 lines in `Color.hpp`, the ImGuiWrapper files, `IMSlider.cpp` and `GLCanvas3D.cpp`. No OrcaSlicer-owned file changed in this round. I haven't rechecked the fixes in the live app yet.

**What changed, by report item**
- **1–3, plate strip, navigator cube, canvas toolbar:** the window hides OrcaSlicer's legacy overlay layer on open and restores it on close, as Prepare does.
- **6 and 16, G-code listing:** the window remembers the app-wide "show G-code window" setting, turns it off on open, and restores it on every close path, which also undoes a C key pressed inside. Turning it on inside the window is left alone until close.
- **8, keyboard focus:** Tab and Shift+Tab now move through canvas, report, Legend and Close, and around. This includes the canvas's own Tab event. Escape closes from any of them.
- **9 and 10, scrolling:** a row selected from the keyboard scrolls into view. A report taller than its panel shows a thin scrollbar: surface-subtle track, border-strong thumb, radius-small. Its width and inset reuse the 4 DIP spacing token, because there is no scrollbar token yet.
- **11, caption:** it sits top-left at the space-3 inset, with the title in the bold font. In a narrow preview it now ends with an ellipsis before OrcaSlicer's legend; the legend reached into that corner in the pictures.
- **12, camera:** the window opens fitted to the slice, and Prepare's own view comes back on close.
- **13, minimum size:** the window can't shrink below 900 × 600 DIP. At that size the sliders, their value boxes and the panel stay apart.
- **14, dark Close button:** header buttons can now take the surface they sit on. Only the Close button uses this; every other button keeps its old surface.
- **15, stale hover:** the window clears ImGui's pointer position when it opens, when the pointer leaves its canvas, and on close. No upstream line was needed.
- **Supports count:** it now reads "1 object · 43 layers", from a new objects count in the fork's support check.

**What the tests prove**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Full build | passes |
| Catch2 report-model tests | 63 assertions pass, including the new scroll and scrollbar arithmetic |
| Agent suite | 15,114 assertions pass |
| `--check-print` harness, light | 169 checks pass |
| `--check-print` harness, dark | passes |
| Default, `--print-issues`, `--print-issue-readers` runs | 566, 484 and 253 checks pass |

With the fixes temporarily undone, the matching harness checks failed, nine in all, including overlays, listing, hover, camera fit, minimum size, the dark Close button, scrollbar and scroll-into-view. I looked at the canvas pictures for default, Legend on, selected finding and minimum size, in light and dark, and at the panel pictures.

**Limits**
- **Focus depends on the app being in front.** macOS only gives keyboard focus to the frontmost app. Real Tab movement was observed and passed in four runs, and logged as unobserved in the others. The Tab order itself is checked every run.
- **Pointer-only behaviour is untested:** wheel scrolling, dragging, hover, clicking rows or Close, and pointer-leave clearing the hover. The harness checks the reset when the window opens, starting from a simulated stale pointer.

The brief, logs, build scripts and pictures are untracked in the worktree root. The light pictures are in `check-print-capture/` and the dark ones in `check-print-capture-dark/`.
